parts.gloss: husband or lord of the shore

literal: Like darkness indeed that watches for the extinction of the lamp, the pallor watches for the end of the husband's embrace.
translation: Just like darkness that waits for the lamp to go out, this pallor waits for the moment my husband's embrace ends to spread over me.
modern: விளக்கு அணையும் தருணத்தை எதிர்பார்த்துக் காத்திருக்கும் இருளைப் போல, தலைவனுடைய அணைப்பு முடியும் தருணத்தை எதிர்பார்த்துக் காத்திருக்கிறது இந்தப் பசலை நிறம்.
explanation: This couplet beautifully illustrates the instantaneous nature of the heroine's grief during separation. She compares the pallor (pasappu) that spreads over her skin to darkness (iruḷ) waiting to engulf a room. Just as darkness watches for the lamp (viḷakku) to be extinguished to immediately take over, the pallor watches for the exact moment her husband's (koṇkaṇ) embrace (muyakku) ends (aṟṟam) to cover her. The comparison highlights how the joy of union is like light, and the pain of separation is like an ever-waiting darkness.
